messages:
sophie: FYI — escalating: Acme reports repeated SSE disconnects that lead to duplicate or truncated completions. Opening ticket INC-2142.

maria (CS): Customer says their client reconnects automatically after short network blips and then resubmits the same request. Sometimes they see duplicated final tokens, other times parsing errors from partial JSON. Frequency ~2-3x/day. Latency otherwise normal.

ajay (eng-runtime): Can you paste the exact client behavior and request headers? Do they send an idempotency header or any resume token?

sophie: Dev sent a minimal repro log. They use an EventSource polyfill and no explicit idempotency header. Example: 
```
connect SSE -> server emits data: {"chunk_id":"c1","text":"Hel"}
network blip -> connection closes
reconnect (same body) -> server emits data: {"chunk_id":"c1","text":"lo"}
client concatenates => "Hello"; but sometimes they get both halves twice or partial fragments
```

linus (eng-platform): If the client immediately retries without dedupe, duplicates are expected unless server supports continuation tokens or idempotency semantics.

maria (CS): They expected the server to resume where it left off automatically.

ajay (eng-runtime): Current behavior: streams are per-connection unless the client provides X-Idempotency-Key or explicitly requests resume with a resume token. We do emit periodic resume markers, but they may be sent as SSE comment lines. Some client libs drop comment lines (leading colon), so they won't see the marker.

sophie: They told us they didn't observe any resume token in their stream, only data lines.

ajay (eng-runtime): Two likely causes: (1) older model variants or runtime paths that emit fewer resume markers; (2) client SSE implementation is stripping comment lines. We use comment lines to avoid interfering with clients that expect only JSON in data fields, but that means some polyfills miss the marker.

linus (eng-platform): Which quick mitigations can we recommend while engineering fixes runtime?

ajay (eng-runtime): Short-term guidance: 
- Instruct the client to include X-Idempotency-Key (UUID) on initial requests and reuse it on reconnects; server will dedupe completed generations when key present.
- Advise the client to implement a small receive buffer: accumulate bytes until a full JSON object (matching braces) is available before parsing; network cuts can split objects.
- Add a client-side dedupe using (generation_hint or chunk_id, sequence_index) to drop repeats.
- Increase reconnect backoff slightly (e.g., 500ms->1s) to reduce races.

maria (CS): Customer tried idempotency key but still hit a case where parser failed on truncated JSON during reconnect.

ajay (eng-runtime): Truncated JSON indicates the client parsed partial data. We emit each chunk as an independent JSON payload per SSE data line, but if the TCP stream splits mid-line and the client tries to parse immediately, it will fail. Buffering until complete objects arrive is essential.

sophie: Customer provided a sanitized capture showing split chunks:
```
data: {"chunk_id":"c2","text":"...conti"
[data cut]
data: {"chunk_id":"c2","text":"nuation","done":true}
```
When they reconnect and re-request, sometimes the server also replays earlier tokens (duplicate emission) because the reconnect hit a different backend with no partial state.

ajay (eng-runtime): I searched logs for correlation_id 0a1b2c3. Root cause: LB failover — the first backend had partial progress buffered; the retry landed on a new backend which started a fresh generation because there was no idempotency header or the resume token was invisible to the client. That produced duplicate final tokens.

linus (eng-platform): Short-term infra options: make LB affinity sticky for SSE connections (cookie or idempotency-key-based stickiness) to reduce cross-backend mismatches. Also consider logging more metadata per chunk for CS lookups.

ajay (eng-runtime): Runtime action plan: 
1) Hotfix (48h): embed resume_token, generation_id, and sequence_index inside the JSON payload (not only as SSE comments). Emit correlation_id on every chunk. Low risk.
2) Near-term (1-2 weeks): honor X-Idempotency-Key for partial progress: keep partial state for 30s, allow resume, and return 409 that references an existing generation when a duplicate intent is detected. Add LB affinity keyed by idempotency key for SSE.
3) Long-term (next sprint): distributed resume service / shared partial-state cache across backends.

maria (CS): Customer is Dedicated/Premium so we can enable short-term protections. They want logs for correlation_id 0a1b2c3.

ajay (eng-runtime): I'll attach redacted logs and include an explanation. I'll also add unit tests to SDKs to ensure SSE comment lines and colon-prefixed markers are handled or embedded in JSON.

sophie: I'll send the workaround to the customer: keep X-Idempotency-Key on reconnects, implement buffering until full JSON objects, and dedupe on (generation_id, sequence_index). Include sample client snippet.

ajay (eng-runtime): example dedupe snippet for customer: 
```
// client-side dedupe
const seen = new Set();
function handleChunk(obj){
  const key = `${obj.generation_id}:${obj.seq}`;
  if (seen.has(key)) return; // drop duplicate
  seen.add(key);
  appendToOutput(obj.text);
}
```

sophie: Customer applied buffering + dedupe and saw big improvement, but one duplicate final token still observed (that was correlation_id 0a1b2c3). We have the logs attached to INC-2142.

linus (eng-platform): I'll open infra ticket to test LB stickiness and estimate rollback plan.

deploy-bot: deploy/streams-hotfix v1.2.3 queued by @ajay — ETA ~40m

sophie: Follow-ups: audit SDKs for SSE comment drop (notably node-eventsource polyfills), update docs recommending resume_token inside JSON payload, and track customer impact metric. Marking INC-2142 for postmortem if duplicates persist. Thanks all! :thumbsup:
